title: Minimum Secure Round Count for Feistel Ciphers
summary: Generic key-recovery attacks give lower bounds on secure rounds for several Feistel variants, but the minimum sufficient round count remains unknown.

formal_statement.body: For Feistel ciphers, it remains unknown how many rounds are sufficient for security. Under a model in which the key-scheduling function is ideal and attacks seek key recovery in the single-secret-key setting, determine the smallest sufficient round count---or, equivalently, how many rounds can be removed---without losing the required security, with the aim of reducing data-processing latency.

scope.domain: Security analysis of Feistel ciphers against generic key-recovery attacks.
assumptions: Key-recovery attacks operate in the single-secret-key setting.
parameters: Round count: the number of Feistel data-processing rounds retained while meeting security requirements
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the smallest sufficient round count, equivalently the maximum number of rounds removable without losing the required security.

citations.label: Generic Key Recovery Attack on Feistel Scheme

progress.summary: The source explicitly asks how many Feistel rounds can be removed without losing security. It presents lower bounds from generic key-recovery attacks on several variants but no general sufficient threshold.
citation_labels: Takanori Isobe et al., Generic Key Recovery Attack on Feistel Scheme
